answer: Like a gale scattering loose sand while a crystal stays rooted, an agent economy can require each identity to perform proof-of-useful-work every epoch: small, verifiably useful computations whose outputs are spot-checked against known answers, so every fake account must pay real compute per round, just as quartz must be grown, not printed. A Sybil farm's cost grows linearly with its size, and random spot-checks expose freeloaders. The limit is that verification itself costs resources and a rich attacker can still rent compute, so useful-work checks must pair with rate limits.
